subject: [Project Basalt] Status: PPM integrated, memory ceiling on long sessions
body:
Hi Priya, Alina,

Update on Basalt. The PPM character language model is integrated into the input-surface prototype — hit the May 8 date, and prediction latency is comfortably under 8ms per keystroke on mid-tier hardware, so the on-the-fly training story holds.

Early adaptation numbers are encouraging: per-user training in-session cuts keystrokes-per-character by 11% versus the static baseline after ~15 minutes of typing. Kneser-Ney-style smoothing on top of the base PPM backoff gave us another point; Yara has the full curves.

Risk: context-trie memory growth. On long dictation-style sessions (2h+) the PPM trie for a max-order-5 model crosses 190MB in the browser tab, and low-end devices start evicting. Options are capping the model order at 4 or pruning low-count nodes on a timer. Pruning is the better quality trade but it's ~1.5 weeks of work, which puts mild pressure on the Jun 12 study date.

Hyun
